paper_metadata.title: Investigate on thermal tensile of Mg-3Gd-0.5Zn alloys containing LPSO phase

evidence.quote: The thermal tensile behavior of the annealed Mg-3Gd-0.5Zn alloy, containing lamellar (long-period stacking ordered, LPSO) phases, was investigated at the same strain rate (2.2 × 10 ⁻⁴ s ⁻ ¹) under different temperatures (100 ◦ C – 200 ◦ C).

The extruded and annealed Mg-3Gd-0.5Zn alloy with a lamellar LPSO phase exhibited a decrease in peak stress and an increase in fracture elongation as temperature increased, but no dynamic recrystallization (DRX) occurred during tensile testing at elevated temperature.

The Mg-3Gd-0.5Zn (wt%) alloy ingot was produced using an in - duction melting furnace and protected by an Ar + SF 6 (99:1) atmosphere.
A cylindrical sample with dimensions of Φ 44 * 40 mm was cut from the ingot ’ s center and homogenized at 530 ◦ C for 24 hours to ensure uniformity.
The homogenized ingot underwent extrusion at a rate of 1 mm/ s and 450 ◦ C using a four-column hydraulic press with an extrusion ratio of 20:1 to achieve a consistent microstructure.
To introduce the LPSO phase into the alloy, the extruded rod received heat treatment at 450 ◦ C for 3 hours in a furnace and was then rapidly cooled in water.
The rod was subsequently processed in the extrusion direction (ED) to produce a tensile sample, as illustrated in Fig. 1 .

The production of significant kink bands and numerous LAGBs in the hot-stretched sample did not result in obvious recrystallization, which is the result of the combined action of too dense LPSO phases and low temperature [48] .
